content.text:
Finding submitted.

**T4C — Termination for convenience: deviation (high).**

- **What the document does:** Article IV (p0049) locks us into a 36-month Initial Period, renewable for seven years *at Licensor's option*. Nothing in Article IV, Article XIX (insolvency), Article XX (change of control / wind-up), Article XXI (effect of termination) or the General Provisions gives Licensee any right to exit without cause. Licensor, by contrast, may terminate immediately on any Licensee breach, on an unconsented Change of Control, and if Licensee winds up.
- **Why it fails:** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule; it does not even reach the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a fee capped at three months' fees). Licensor holds no convenience right, so no deletion is required.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** new clause IV inserted after p0049 — Licensee may terminate for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, without penalty, with refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period. Comment offers 60 days' notice as a landing zone.
